name: Lunar Orbiter
goal: Map the Moon in detail so future crews can pick safe landing sites and find water ice.
objectives: Map surface features at high resolution
Measure surface temperature day and night
Measure the radiation environment for future crews

texts.cruise: A short five-day trip to the Moon begins.
texts.insertion: A burn of about 555 m/s slows the craft into a low polar orbit around the Moon.
texts.shadow: On the first pass behind the Moon, the arrays went dark and there was no battery. The spacecraft lost power.

brief: The real orbiter carried about 92 kg of science instruments, out of about 1,846 kg at launch. (NASA GSFC mission design paper; NASA NSSDC)
fuelNote: Propellant, not gasoline: the real orbiter used hydrazine for its orbit burns. (NTRS 20180000056)
dvNote: Total Δv about 1,258 m/s, including 555 m/s for lunar orbit insertion (NTRS 20110007093).

resReal.mass: 1 unit ≈ 9.2 kg. The real orbiter weighed about 1,846 kg at launch (NASA GSFC mission design paper).
resReal.power: 1 unit ≈ 8.2 W. The real orbiter averaged about 823 W in orbit (NTRS 20180000056).
resReal.data: 1 unit ≈ 1 Mbps. The real orbiter sent up to 100 Mbps in Ka band (NTRS 20180000056; one source only).
resReal.prop: 1 unit ≈ 9.8 kg of hydrazine. The real orbiter carried about 894 kg of fuel (NTRS 20180000056).
resReal.budget: 1 unit = $1 million. LRO’s real cost was not found in a NASA source, so this budget is a game value.

name: Mars Orbiter
goal: Find where water once shaped Mars, and scout safe sites for future landers.
objectives: Image candidate landing sites at high resolution
Identify water-related minerals on the surface

texts.cruise: Cruise toward Mars begins: about seven months in space.
texts.insertion: Six thrusters fire for about 25 minutes. Captured into Mars orbit.
texts.shadow: On the first pass through Mars’ shadow, the arrays went dark and there was no battery. The spacecraft lost power.

brief: The real orbiter carried about 139 kg of science instruments out of 2,180 kg at launch. Every gram of camera needed propellant to carry it. (JPL MRO press kit)
fuelNote: Propellant, not gasoline: the real orbiter carried hydrazine in a 1,220 kg tank and used about 70% of it to enter Mars orbit. (JPL MRO press kit)
dvNote: About 1,000 m/s for Mars orbit insertion (JPL MRO press kit), plus 400 m/s for other burns (game assumption).

resReal.mass: 1 unit ≈ 10.9 kg. The real orbiter weighed 2,180 kg at launch (JPL MRO press kit).
resReal.power: 1 unit ≈ 20 W. The real arrays gave about 2,000 W at Mars (JPL MRO press kit).
resReal.data: 1 unit ≈ 0.06 Mbps. The real orbiter could send up to 6 Mbps (JPL MRO press kit).
resReal.prop: 1 unit ≈ 12.2 kg of hydrazine. The real tank held 1,220 kg (JPL MRO press kit).
resReal.budget: 1 unit = $1 million. The real mission cost about $720 million (JPL MRO press kit).

name: Mars Lander
goal: Land safely on Mars and listen to its interior: marsquakes, heat flow and the planet’s wobble.
objectives: Record marsquakes to map the interior
Measure heat escaping from inside the planet
sunlight: About 43% of Earth’s, less when dust settles on the arrays

texts.cruise: Cruise toward Mars begins inside the protective aeroshell: about six and a half months.
texts.insertion: The heat shield glows through entry, the parachute opens, and the descent engines set the lander softly on the ground.
texts.shadow: The first Martian night drained the spacecraft with no battery to keep it warm and powered. The lander was lost.
texts.propFail: The descent engines ran dry before touchdown, and the lander hit the ground too fast.

brief: InSight weighed about 694 kg at launch. Its two round solar arrays give about 600 to 700 W on a clear Martian day, and only 200 to 300 W when dust covers them. Its heat shield was slightly thicker than Phoenix’s. (JPL InSight press kit)
fuelNote: Landers need propellant for the final descent after the parachute. A bigger parachute slows the lander more, so less propellant is needed.
dvNote: Descent Δv values and the parachute savings are game assumptions; they were not in the NASA pages opened.

real.cost: not confirmed in a NASA source
real.instruments: seismometer, heat probe, radio science, arm and cameras, weather sensors

resReal.mass: 1 unit ≈ 4 kg. InSight weighed about 694 kg at launch (JPL InSight press kit).
resReal.power: 1 unit ≈ 6.5 W. InSight’s arrays give about 600–700 W on a clear Martian day (JPL InSight press kit).
resReal.data: Game units only: a NASA data rate for InSight was not in the pages opened.
resReal.prop: 1 unit ≈ 1.2 kg of descent propellant. Game value.
resReal.budget: 1 unit = $1 million. A NASA figure for InSight’s total cost was not confirmed in the sources opened, so this budget is a game value.

board: Earth to the surface of Mars

name: Europa Flyby Explorer
goal: Find out whether places below Europa’s icy surface could support life. This is not a life-detection mission.
objectives: Measure the thickness of the ice shell
Detect the ocean through the induced magnetic field

texts.cruise: A 5.5-year cruise begins, with gravity assists from Mars and Earth.
texts.insertion: A long engine burn captures the spacecraft into orbit around Jupiter.
texts.shadow: In Jupiter’s shadow the arrays went dark and there was no battery. The spacecraft lost power.

brief: Europa Clipper weighed about 6,000 kg at launch, and about 2,750 kg of that was propellant. Its arrays span about 102 m² to catch weak sunlight at Jupiter. (europa.nasa.gov; JPL Europa Clipper quick facts)
fuelNote: Almost half of the real spacecraft’s launch mass was propellant: about 2,750 kg of about 6,000 kg. (europa.nasa.gov)
dvNote: Δv values for this mission are game assumptions; NASA pages opened did not give them. Isp 223 s is the hydrazine value from NTRS 19970010493.

resReal.mass: 1 unit ≈ 30 kg. Europa Clipper weighed about 6,000 kg at launch (europa.nasa.gov).
resReal.power: 1 unit ≈ 7 W. Its arrays give at least 700 W at Jupiter (JPL Europa Clipper spacecraft page).
resReal.data: Game units only: the NASA pages opened did not give Europa Clipper’s data rate.
resReal.prop: 1 unit ≈ 30 kg. About 2,750 kg of propellant at launch (europa.nasa.gov).
resReal.budget: 1 unit = $10 million. The full mission costs about $5.2 billion over its life (JPL Europa Clipper quick facts).

board: Earth to Jupiter, with gravity assists
